Class SessionRegistry

java.lang.Object
com.sbancuz.offscreen.core.SessionRegistry
public final class SessionRegistry extends Object
Tracks live Sessions by owning window for client maintenance and closure. Sessions normally dispose and untrack themselves; world unload calls disposeAll() to release all remaining bindings.

The concurrent map tolerates removal during tick/disposal loops. Session lifecycle methods still belong on the client thread. Register at most one live session per window; replacing a map entry does not dispose the old session.

  • Method Details

    • track

      public void track(Session session)
      Associates a session with its window, replacing any previous association.
      Parameters:
      session - non-null session with a non-null owning window

    • untrack

      public void untrack(Session session)
      Removes ownership only if the window still belongs to this exact session. An old session finishing teardown cannot remove a newer replacement.
      Parameters:
      session - association to remove

    • get

      @Nullable public Session get(@Nullable Window window)
      Finds the session that currently owns a window.
      Parameters:
      window - window to inspect; null matches nothing
      Returns:
      associated session, or null

    • find

      @Nullable public Session find(@Nullable Predicate<Session> filter)
      Searches sessions in unspecified iteration order.
      Parameters:
      filter - match rule; null matches nothing; exceptions propagate
      Returns:
      first accepted session encountered, or null

    • tickAll

      public void tickAll()
      Runs one maintenance tick per encountered session. Logs failures separately so one broken integration does not prevent other sessions from updating. The failed session is not automatically removed by this method.

    • disposeAll

      public void disposeAll()
      Attempts every session's teardown, logs failures, then clears all associations. Called when leaving a world so server bindings cannot leak into the next world.
